newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1996 CPI below 18 pct within reach - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1996 CPI below 18 pct within reach - IMF.

text.p: Polish inflation has a chance of falling below 18 percent in 1996 but no sharp decline in price should be expected, Poland's senior International Monetary Fund (IFM) representative told The Warsaw Voice weekly.
"This year's inflation in Poland should come below 18 percent and this is within reach," Markus Rodlauer told the English-language paper in an interview.
The official government 1996 inflation target is 17 percent, while banks expect year-on-year price growth to slow to 18.6 percent in December. @

Rodlauer said gradual reduction of Poland's inflation, running at 20.5 percent year-on-year in August, was more likely than an immediate sharp reduction in price growth because of several structual problems Poland faced.
He said the wage growth mechanism which indexes salaries to price growth created a direct link between the two and hampered government attempts to lower the inflation.
Inflation was also fuelled by unreformed sectors of the economy, which often increase prices to compensate for high costs instead of modernising, he said. @

"Often an enterprise that is not able to reform tries to push the resulting costs onto its prices...(and) many of these sectors and industries have some monopoly power or enjoy protection," Rodlauer said.
